title: Limitations of AI
author: Financial-Metal-7702
selftext: Is it possible to make a 3D open-world game using AI + unity even with little game development knowledge? I'm a mobile dev and I want to start a game project in the style of Aniimo, but with a few extra layers of complexity in the abilities, and I don't know if it's actually possible to build a project doing almost everything with AI. I saw videos of people creating assets and got excited, but maybe it's just FOMO.

comments.author: ajarOfSalt
comments.body: Honestly anything is possible at this point with enough compute and determination.

replies.author: takshit2
replies.body: I agree. and AI is getting smarter like every month. One day, someone with no dev knowledge can make an entire game with enough knowledge how to use AI.

replies.author: Ok_Improvement_8735
replies.body: Fun fact, before AI with just a few months of working with IDEs and programming languages, anything felt possible with enough compute and determination without spending money with cycling AI prompts as you iterate through your project.

comments.author: pikachuswayless
comments.body:
You will still have to do a lot of work if you don't want the game to look and feel like trash. If you're not prepared to put in the work/time (and tokens) to polish the game, your game will end up with the "slop" label.

Yes it's possible to make a 3D open-world game using AI + unity even with little game development knowledge. But making a good 3D open-world game takes much more work.

replies.author: Financial-Metal-7702
replies.body: Yes, I'm ready to get my hands dirty with the code. I use AI a lot in development nowadays and I'm an experienced dev, but since I don't have a background in game development, I was wondering if this would be possible. I know that physics, design, and other areas are pretty complex—much more than a complex mobile app—hence the concern

replies.author: ipreuss
replies.body:
In my experience, code isn’t the problem. For me, the three main areas of work are

\- game design  
\- asset generation  
\- a maintainable (by AI) architecture

comments.author: thygrrr
comments.body:
Sure it's possible, it's only going to be a fairly bland or janky game, though.

You cannot make a decent game without the skills and understanding of what makes a good game, and how that game works under the hood, including its creation.

replies.author: LucidFir
replies.body: What DOES make a good game? The question I've got is; "if I've got a gameplay mechanic I enjoy, how do I then give progression and rewards and goals, or is there some other way to give purpose?"

replies.author: Jolva
replies.body: I think someone with a mobile developer background is going to have knowledge about basic programming best practices, source control, etc so you're already better off than the average person. If you also have taste, that's a huge flex that a lot of people simply don't have. If you a unique idea that you've put actual thought into, along with everything else, then you have everything you need.

comments.author: geldonyetich
comments.body:
Think of it as asking someone else to do it for you.

This particular someone else is a robot, so you're going to have to bridge the gap a little more to ground it in human reality.

But the difference is if you don't really understand how to do the subject matter itself, you're going to possibly overestimate your knowledge, not know what to look for, or have the skills to touch it up yourself.

But I am not saying don't do it. I am saying be aware of the limitations and adapt accordingly.

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body: Best analogy ever, I still have to make iterations to another human artist to the point they tretenen me to spend more or stop iterating, ai is more or less the same, but way cheaper then a human.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Technically you eventually can with no guarantee tho because nobody could ever bring this experience yet as this is kinda a novelty to have AI at this level. You maybe could get there but maybe your project will reach a limit that you wont be able to solve without a seasoned professional programmer and developer or your project might even reach a disastrous dead end because the architecture of your project is a disaster.   
  
Nonetheless just because AI is powerful nowadays dont get fooled by the enthusiasm and ambitions coming from it. The scope creep is real and AI doesnt solve that. You will end up spending years upon years of development if unless you drastically compromise and you will have to setup a workflow with AI agents that is far more detailed than you maybe imagine given all these people showing those prototypes on social media. You will ideally spend hours, days, weeks to properly setup the environment for AI agents in the first place and THEN you will have an expensive team of AI agents workforce that will slow down your game development a lot for the sake of quality of your game and very importantly also entire architecture of your code and system so your game doesnt break and reach a architectural armageddon. That also means you will spend a lot of money and thats before we even talk about serious marketing, eventually buying assets (because trust me letting AI doing those properly will take many hours as well, weeks, months). 

Do not get blinded by enthusiasm and hype no matter how powerful AI is or people make it to be, actual production and professional approach to game development as a business is a whole different league than what people present with Astra and Opus on social media.

comments.author: Alternative-Shame147
comments.body: The problem isn't the open world itself, but its content. You can create an open world of any size, but if there’s nothing to do in it, the game won’t be engaging. You can scatter assets across a map without any programming or AI. The real issue lies in game design: do you have an idea that will truly captivate the player?

comments.author: FazedEclipse2
comments.body:
I started this process with the idea that I could build an entire RPG from scratch with the assistance of AI...then I received my first vertical slice and realised...actually I have a lot of work on here.

So then I looked at my limitations vs what is achievable, what I had an understanding of and eventually after about a week I had a first person dragon quest esque battle system with story elements and comic book style cuts across the screen showing the characters and enemies doing attacks. It was pretty sick.

Experimenting with little projects that might work with in a bigger project.

I noticed a huge flaw...straying from the plan meant the plan became mutated beyond my vision. AI would bring up game systems I didnt want anymore, offer solutions to problems I had already told it the answer to.

The solution, make the plan yourself. Create your story, art style, as much content written as you can, highlight the gameplay mechanics and how they can work in your game engine of choice...once you are happy...dont build a verticle slice. Build the back end. Put your vertical slice on top of already provable working systems, dont build the systems as you build the game out, it wont work out well for you.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Possible. But it comes down to time, willpower and money. The videos people put out make it seem like you can drop a real ass AAA game in a month. They one-shot a snapshot clone of something and go, "Oh with another week of effort this could totally be a playable game." Yet the fact none of them have actually made a full ass game from their tech demos should be a good indicator of the truth of things. AI can get you there, but it's still a huge process. Years worth of dev time if you're starting from zero experience.

comments.author: Aggressive_Bike3881
comments.body:
The biggest problem isn’t if it’s possible. It is. The biggest problem is to make sure it is able to resist accusations of slop as much as it is possible ( some will de facto call it slop if AI was involved somehow even if it is code assisted).

And you just have to be ok with this.
